checks: No eclipse at 1 of 6 covered epochs where the 4.85885 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 342569756 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 4.8589 days. The primary eclipse causes a dimming of 28.50%, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal stands out strongly in TESS photometry data, with a detection significance of 628.0 in the Box Least Squares search. Pixel-level analysis using difference imaging confirms the signal at the target location, though with a centroid offset of 1.8 arcsec. The system does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel candidate. The machine learning screening score of 0.34 indicates moderate confidence that this represents a real eclipsing system rather than instrumental noise or artifact.
